en.html:
Prison life had three musicians: monotony, loneliness, and being shut in. Same three, same performance. Any age, any world, I suspected the concert would be much the same.

Still, this could not go on forever...

Kanae had her private reasons. GHQ must have its own reasons for keeping me on this base. No army collected prisoners simply to have a collection.

Keeping me in a cage and feeding me like a pet could hardly be the final purpose. Sooner or later, some approach would come.

Lekin when? It was taking its own time.

Under these conditions, whatever broke the monotony was welcome. Anything at all.

ja.html:
幽閉生活というものはおおむね単調と孤独と閉塞の
三重奏に支配される。
　これは何処の世界のどんな時代でもまず変わらない
真理であろう。

　この状態がいつまでも続くとは思えないのだが……。
　俺がこうしてＧＨＱの基地内に囚われている事には、
香奈枝嬢の私的事情とは別にＧＨＱの事情がなくては
おかしい。無意味に虜囚を取る軍はない。

　その事情が、俺を愛玩動物よろしく檻に入れて餌を
与え続けること自体を目的としているとは考えられな
かった。
　必ず何らかのアプローチはしてくるだろう。

　しかし――それがなかなか訪れない。
　そんな日々において、単調さを崩してくれる要素の
到来は何であれ歓迎すべきものだった。

en.html:
When the Anglo-Saxons entered another country, they built their own country inside it. So people often said.

Not the same as overseas Chinese building a Chinatown. People who had moved abroad for trade made a base, a copy of home, somewhere to find peace. That was its purpose. Once the necessary surroundings were complete, the expansion stopped. Enough for living; bas, enough.

An Anglo-Saxon city kept growing.

A limit was not part of the arrangement.

Occupy a country by force: destroy or take its culture and civilization, then build cities according to your own. Establish trade: export your culture and civilization until the other city also starts looking like home.

Conquerors in the full meaning. Great Britain—the British Commonwealth, their parent state—controlled more than half the world politically. Its cultural reach was surely greater still.

Yamato could not stand aside and say, not our problem. A hundred years since the Tokugawa regime fell—the regime that had restricted foreign trade to protect domestic industry and culture. Now motorcars filled the streets. Railroads joined the cities.

Some people saw danger and sounded the alarm. Ishima Sakon-no-Shougen, who wrote On Selling the Nation, was one of quite a few. But more people accepted the changes. Welcomed them. In one respect, they were helping the invasion of their own country. Khud, with their own hands.

And there was a reason.

Invention founded on rationalism: at that, the Anglo-Saxons excelled. In many fields, the convenience of what they made left the other cultures unable to catch up. Faster. Bigger. Stronger.

People wanted it. So it spread.

There was the difficulty, bhai. Try shouting 'Go back!' at a thing which made the journey quicker. Go back, certainly—but first tell us how to make ours go this fast. And leave the spare parts. Freedom must not be stranded halfway because we have thrown away the useful spanner. A most efficient conquest: even the objection wanted to travel by the conqueror's railway.

Strip away every pleasing word, every scrap of romance, and in that blunt sense they were the superior people. Superior people, superior scientific civilization. They believed bringing it to distant backwaters was justice. And if justice was on their side, hesitation was unnecessary.

From that reasoning, the Anglo-Saxon empire's triumph looked inevitable.

ja.html:
アングロ・サクソン族は他国に進出すると、そこに
<ruby>自国<rt>・・</rt></ruby>を形成する――しばしばそう評される。

　それは華僑が中華街を造るのとは異なる。
　商業目的で他国に移住した彼ら華僑が築造する街は、
拠点であると同時に故郷の写し――安息の地であるが、
そこまでのものに過ぎない。

　拠点であり故郷である中華街は発展の限界を持つ。
　自分達の生活に必要充分な環境が完成すれば、それ
から更に規模を拡大していく事はない。

　アングロサクソンの都市は拡大する。
　際限なく。

　軍事的に占領した国では現地の文化文明を破壊また
は強奪しつつ自国の文化文明に沿って都市化する。
　交易関係を結んだ国へは、自国の文化文明を積極的
に輸出し、やがて都市の様相を自国化する。

　彼らは真の意味における征服者だ。
　アングロサクソン族の宗主国家といえる<ruby>大英連邦<rt>グレート・ブリテン</rt></ruby>は
政治的に世界の過半を制しているが、文化的な版図は
きっと更に広かろう。

　無論、大和にとっても他人事などではない。
　国内の産業と文化を保護するため諸外国との交易に
制限を掛けていた徳川政体が遂に打倒されて以来百年。
今や市街には<ruby>自動車<rt>モーターカー</rt></ruby>が行き交い、都市間は<ruby>鉄道<rt>レールロード</rt></ruby>が繋ぐ。

　そうした変化に危惧を抱き、警鐘を鳴らす人間も、
『売国論』を著した<ruby>石馬左近将監<rt>いしまさこんのしょうげん</rt></ruby>など少なからずいる。
　しかし、より多くの人々が変化を受け入れ、歓迎し、
一面において自国侵略の一助をなしているのだった。

　そしてそうなるからには、相応の理由が存在した。
　アングロサクソン族は合理主義に基づく発明に長け、
その文化の利便性は多くの方面で他文化の追随を許さ
ない。彼らが造る物は速く、<ruby>巨<rt>おおき</rt></ruby>く、強い。

　だからこそ求められ、普及する。

　最も身も蓋も味も素っ気もない意味において彼らは
他に優越する種族なのである。

　優秀なる彼らは優秀な科学文明を持ち、その文明を
僻地へもたらす正義を信じ、正義ゆえに躊躇わない。
　アングロサクソン帝国の覇業が成るのは必然と云う
べきであろう。

Kageaki"Even if Rokuhara brought its whole strength, could it take this base? I have my doubts. First, we would have to cut it off from Yokosuka..."
Kanae"That is so..."
Kageaki"..."

en.html:
Small talk, that had been my intention. But today Kanae's replies were arriving without much of her attached. Just vague agreement.

Had a prisoner inspecting and criticizing the base so freely finally worn out her patience? Perhaps. But it did not seem like that.

Looking at her face, I could not be sure the conversation was even reaching her.

ja.html:
世間話のつもりで話を振ってみたが、どうも香奈枝
嬢の反応はいつになく鈍い。
　生返事を寄越してくるばかりだった。

　捕虜でありながら遠慮もなく周囲を検分し批評する
態度が呆れを買ったのかとも思ったが、違うようだ。
　顔色を窺うに、そもそも話がまともに聞かれている
かどうかからして疑わしい。

Kageaki"Captain."
Kanae"..."
Kageaki"Are you perhaps feeling unwell...?"
Kanae"...Hm?"
Kanae"Ah, yes. I was thinking the same."
Kageaki"As I feared. Then please take care of yourself. For me, with nothing to do, the invitation was welcome. But that does not mean you must strain yourself on my account. No need to go to such lengths."
Kanae"Hm?"
Kageaki"Then we should return at once. To be safe, the army doctor—"
Sayo"Minato sir, itna alarm is not required just yet. She will be all right."
Kageaki"But—"
Sayo"Madam. Your mind appeared to have gone elsewhere. Minato sir became concerned."
Sayo"He was asking whether you are unwell. ...Any complaint from the health department?"
Kanae"...Ah."
Kanae"No, no, forgive me, Kageaki. As you see, there is plenty of life in me."
Kageaki"Truly?"
Kanae"Haan, too much life! Everywhere, full power—quite a problem. Kageaki, you would like a demonstration...?"

景明「大尉殿」
香奈枝「……」
景明「もしや、御身体の具合でも……」
香奈枝「……え？」
香奈枝「あ、はい。わたくしもそう思いましてよ」
景明「やはり。ならば御自愛下さい。 　確かに無聊をかこつ自分には有難いお誘い でしたが、大尉殿にそのような無理までして 頂くには及びません」
香奈枝「え？」
景明「すぐに戻りましょう。 　念のため、軍医に――」
さよ「まぁまぁ湊斗さま。 　そう慌てなくとも、大丈夫でございますよ」
景明「しかし」
さよ「お嬢さま？ 　湊斗さまはお嬢さまが心ここにあらぬ態で おられたのをご心配なさったのです」
さよ「それでおからだの不調を問われたのですが ……何か、健康に思わしからぬところでも？」
香奈枝「……あっ」
香奈枝「いえ、申し訳ありません、景明さま。 　わたくし、この通りピンピンしておりまし てよ」
景明「本当ですか」
香奈枝「ええっ、もー、どこもかしこもビンビンで 困っちゃいます。 　景明さま、ご覧になりたいの……？」

en.html:
Sayo"Well, she will recover in time, I expect."
Kageaki"Yes."
Sayo"That aside, Minato sir. I hear you met Professor Wolf?"
Kageaki"Yes. He invited me to his room, and we spoke briefly."
Sayo"What did you discuss? So far as there is no difficulty in disclosing it, of course."
Kageaki"...Let me see. The strongest impression, for the moment..."
Kageaki"The word 'grammar' was coming up again and again. Quite remarkably often."
Sayo"............"
Sayo"Ah. Difficulty for the listener, then. No shortage on the speaker's side."
Kageaki"My apologies."
Sayo"No, this is his regular condition. What twisted upbringing manufactured such a man, I cannot say. Grammar appears to have him by the throat."
Sayo"Before anything else is said, there it comes: grammar, grammar—"
Kageaki"Madam. On this point, no misunderstanding, please."
Sayo"Hm?"
Kageaki"Grammar is not his obsession. Destroying grammar is his obsession."

en.html:
An open space, apparently a drill ground. Without deciding to, I had stopped walking.

A little over ten people stood there. None of them seemed about to begin a drill.

Most showed no expression.
One had no expression left.

Same appearance, different matter. The others were deliberately hiding theirs. In that one man, expression itself had gone.

His arms were bound. They undid the bonds—or so I thought. Then they were tying his whole body to a stake.

An open space, apparently a drill ground. Without deciding to, I had stopped walking.

A little over ten people stood there. None of them seemed about to begin a drill.

Most showed no expression.
One had no expression left.

Same appearance, different matter. The others were deliberately hiding theirs. In that one man, expression itself had gone.

His arms were bound. They undid the bonds—or so I thought. Then they were tying his whole body to a stake.

演習場らしき広場がある。
　ふと、俺は足を止めていた。

　十人余りの人の群れが見える。
　しかし皆、これから演習という様子ではない。

　多くは無表情であった。
　うち一人は、表情が消えていた。

　両者は似ているようで違う。
　一名は表情というものが欠落してしまったのであり、
他の人々は意図的に表情を隠しているのだ。

　表情の消えた一名は、両腕を拘束されていた。
　それを、解かれた……と思えば、今度は杭に全身を
縛り付けられていく。
